Subject: RE: Sudden 5xx and latency spike in our region (us-east-1 AZ2)

Short update from infra/serving: we see correlated spikes in KV cache eviction and GPU memory pressure on the us-east-1 AZ2 hosts serving the rl-ensemble-13 series for Amberlane traffic. Probable chain: a noisy client pattern (long context generation) amplified KVC misses -> sustained memory pressure -> slightly degraded batching which pushed tail latency and triggered 5xx on overloaded lanes.

What I recommend now (order matters):
1) Gradual traffic repath: shift 40% of Amberlane's routed QPS from us-east-1 AZ2 -> us-east-2 for the next 15 minutes, observe p95 and 5xx. If stable, do another 40% then the remaining 20%. This avoids abrupt cold-starts and keeps KV warm for critical prefixes.
2) On hosts in AZ2, toggle the kvcache-sizing profile to the conservative fallback (profile: small-prefill) to immediately lower eviction churn — this will reduce throughput but should reduce errors.
3) Enable a temporary model-variant fallback (rl-ensemble-13 -> rl-ensemble-13-quant-lite) for non-critical paths to ease GPU load; this will slightly change latency but keeps success rates up.
4) Request AWS assistance to prioritize network egress and to confirm no underlying fabric issue in AZ2 (cc'd aws-cloudops).

ETA for step 1 (repast 40%): I can trigger via routing-controller in ~6 minutes once ops confirms the exact VIPs. I recommend we also prepare a customer-facing note and an SLA credit draft.

Logs I pulled: amberlane/request_samples_08-14-08-03-08-25.log (linked in Drive).

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick customer update from Redwood: we have identified a serving pressure pattern affecting us-east-1 AZ2 that is increasing tail latency and 5xx. Our infra team is executing a staged traffic repath to us-east-2 and activating a temporary lower-memory model variant for certain non-critical endpoints. Expected customer-facing impact: reconnection window for ~5 minutes during each repath stage; we expect p95 to return near baseline within ~25–40 minutes if the plan executes smoothly.

- Draft an SLA one-time credit that we can confirm with you by EOD; included a preliminary credit draft attached.

Subject: Incident summary & executive ask — Amberlane AZ2 outage (RT-7843)

Lucia / Amberlane execs —

Thanks for your patience. Quick executive summary and asks:

What happened: a surge in long-context generation requests caused disproportionate KV cache churn on our us-east-1 AZ2 serving lane, which coupled with GPU memory pressure produced elevated tail latency and 5xx rates between ~08:03–09:30 PT.

What we did: staged traffic repath to us-east-2 completed by 09:45 PT with progressive 40/40/20 shifts; temporary model fallback enabled for non-critical endpoints; conservative kvcache profile applied to AZ2 hosts to stop eviction amplification. P95 returned to ~140ms for Amberlane by 09:50 PT; 5xx fell below 0.5% by 10:05 PT.

Current status: system stable; we are monitoring for recurrence and collecting post-incident telemetry.

Executive asks:
- Approve an immediate make-whole one-time credit (proposed in attached draft) for visible customer impact. Vanessa — ready to sign off?
- Ops/Infra: please run the postmortem timeline and a small-scale replay of the noisy client traffic pattern to validate the kvcache thresholds (Jira: RT-7843).
- Sales leadership: flag Amberlane in the account dashboard as "at-risk" until we complete a 7-day stabilizer and confirm model/traffic guardrails.

We will follow up with a formal postmortem and remediation plan in 48 hours.

—Markus
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
